sections.h2: Where is Florence, Alabama, and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Florence is the county seat of Lauderdale County, in the northwest corner of Alabama on the Tennessee River. It sits about 70 miles west of Huntsville on US-72 and about 115 miles northwest of Birmingham.

The city covers roughly 27 square miles and sits at about 604 feet above sea level. Florence is the largest of the four Shoals cities, which also include Muscle Shoals, Sheffield and Tuscumbia. Together they counted 148,779 people in the 2020 census, and the city is considered the economic hub of northwest Alabama.

For a seller, the practical point is that Florence has a clear downtown grid near the river, older neighborhoods around the University of North Alabama, and newer subdivisions farther out along US-43 and US-72. Each part tends to attract a different kind of buyer, so the way you sell often depends on where the house sits.

sections.h2: What is the history behind Florence's housing stock?
sections.html:
Florence was laid out in 1818 and incorporated in 1826, so some neighborhoods hold houses that are well over a century old. The town plan came from an Italian engineer, Ferdinand Sannoner, who surveyed it in 1819 and named it after Florence, Italy. He put the town on a plateau above the Tennessee River, partly for protection from flooding.

That older core matters when you sell. Houses built long ago often have original wiring, plumbing and foundations that a bank appraiser or an FHA or VA inspector will flag. The 2020 census counted 19,710 housing units in Florence, and 11.1 percent were vacant, so a good number of owners are carrying a second property or an empty one.

  • Founded March 12, 1818, and incorporated January 7, 1826
  • Frank Lloyd Wright's Rosenbaum House, built in 1939, is the only Wright home in Alabama
  • The Florence Indian Mound, built in the Woodland period, is the largest surviving earthen mound in the state

sections.h2: What does the economy look like for Florence homeowners?
sections.html:
Florence is a college and services town. The University of North Alabama is based here, and the city is the commercial center for the Shoals area. Florence City Schools runs the public K-12 system, with Florence High School, Florence Middle School and the Florence Freshman Center.

The American Community Survey for 2023 puts the median household income at $50,396 and says 31.1 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree or higher. About 19.3 percent of residents live at or below the poverty line. Those numbers show a mixed market: some owners have equity and options, and others cannot afford large repairs before a sale.

sections.h2: How does Florence's climate affect a house?
sections.html:
Florence has a humid subtropical climate with hot, humid summers and mild to cool winters. The average temperature is 59 degrees, and the city gets about 57 inches of rain a year plus a little over two inches of snow.

Moisture is the main concern for older houses. Crawl spaces, roof valleys, gutters and window frames take a beating from that much rain. Florence is almost 300 miles from the Gulf, but the path of Hurricane Katrina passed close in 2005 and brought winds near 70 miles per hour. Wind and storm damage are part of the local picture, and a roof that has seen several seasons of storms is a common reason a listing stalls.

  • Check the roof, gutters and flashing before listing, since buyers and inspectors look there first
  • Look at the crawl space and grading for standing water
  • Ask an insurance agent about wind and hail coverage if you are keeping the house for a while

sections.h2: How do roads, transit and the airport shape buyer demand in Florence?
sections.html:
US-43 and US-72 run together through Florence, and both cross the Tennessee River on the O'Neal Bridge to Sheffield. State routes 13, 17, 20, 133 and 157 also serve the city. Florence does not have a direct interstate link, and the closest option is Interstate 65 reached through Alabama 157 to Cullman.

There is no fixed-route bus. The Northwest Alabama Council of Local Governments runs a dial-a-ride service called NACOLG Transit. Commercial flights leave from Northwest Alabama Regional Airport in Muscle Shoals, where Contour Airlines flies to Charlotte, and Huntsville International Airport is about an hour away.

Because most residents drive, houses near the main highways and close to the university or downtown tend to be easier to market than those in remote spots.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Florence?
sections.html:
Alabama charges a recordation tax of 50 cents for each $500 of value on a deed, under Alabama Code 40-22-1. A $150,000 sale would carry $150 in deed tax, plus the recording fee the probate office charges.

The deed is recorded with the judge of probate, and the instrument must come with a form that states the actual purchase price. If someone intentionally fails to provide that proof after being asked, the penalty is $100 or 25 percent of the tax due, whichever is greater. Some deeds with only nominal consideration, used to correct title, are exempt.

  • Deed tax: $0.50 per $500 or fraction of value
  • Filed with the Lauderdale County probate office
  • Value statement required with the deed
  • Probate staff cannot prepare a deed, so an attorney or title company drafts it

sections.h2: When are Florence property taxes due, and what happens at closing?
sections.html:
Alabama property tax is assessed locally at the county courthouse. The Department of Revenue says the lien date is October 1 and the taxes are due the following October 1, and they become delinquent after December 31.

Because of that cycle, a sale in the spring or summer usually means the seller's share of the bill has to be settled at closing. Ask the title company to prorate taxes and confirm the current year is paid before the deed is signed. Unpaid taxes follow the property, not the person.

Owner-occupied property is assessed in Alabama's lowest class, at 10 percent of value. Your county tax office can confirm the exact amount for your parcel.

sections.h2: What choices does a Florence seller have?
sections.html:
A Florence seller can list with an agent, sell privately, or accept a cash offer from an investor. Each has trade-offs in time, cost and certainty.

  • Listing with an agent usually brings the widest pool of buyers, but it means showings, repairs, a commission and a financing contingency that can fall through.
  • A private sale saves the commission but puts marketing, paperwork and negotiation on you.
  • A cash sale can close on your timeline and the buyer takes the house as it stands, which helps with inherited property, tired rentals and houses that need work.

Cash Home Buyers makes offers on Florence houses in their current condition. You decide whether the number works, and there is no obligation to accept.

sections.h2: What does a Florence sale look like when the house needs work?
sections.html:
Houses that need major repairs are common in older parts of town, and they are the hardest to sell on the retail market. Lenders want a house that appraises and passes inspection, and many buyers cannot absorb a repair bill on top of a down payment.

When an owner passed away, the house may also sit empty while the family sorts out the estate. In that case, you should talk with a probate attorney about who has authority to sign. A buyer can only close once the right person can convey title.

  • Gather the deed, any mortgage payoff letter and recent tax bill
  • List what is broken and what works so the buyer can price accurately
  • Ask the title company how liens or unpaid taxes will be cleared at closing

faqs.q: Can I sell my house in Florence, AL as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer takes the house in its current condition and prices the repairs in. Talk to a title company or attorney about what you need to tell any buyer before closing.

faqs.q: How much is the deed tax when selling in Florence?
faqs.a: Alabama's recordation tax is 50 cents for each $500 of value, so a $200,000 sale carries $200 in deed tax before the recording fee. The probate office calculates the amount when the deed is filed.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Lauderdale County?
faqs.a: Alabama taxes are due October 1 and are delinquent after December 31. If you sell during the year, the title company normally prorates the bill at closing.

faqs.q: Do I need an attorney to sell my Florence house?
faqs.a: A title company or attorney usually handles the closing and the deed. The probate office cannot prepare a deed for you, so someone licensed has to do that part.

faqs.q: How fast can a cash sale close in Florence?
faqs.a: The timeline depends on title work and any estate or lien issues. A clean title can close in a matter of weeks, while probate and unpaid liens take longer.

faqs.q: Does the University of North Alabama affect which buyers I will see?
faqs.a: It can. Houses near campus attract investors and families tied to the school, while farther-out subdivisions draw more owner-occupant buyers.
